query: For high-entropy alloys intended as intermediate materials in plasma-facing reactor components, what single intervention could improve heat-transfer capability while preserving structural integrity? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the expected outcome compared with current intermediate-layer performance, the temperature and loading conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: High-entropy alloy intermediate layers processed via directional solidification followed by aligned thermo-mechanical treatment will develop an interconnected, lamellar microstructure that enhances directional heat transfer while preserving mechanical strength under plasma-facing reactor conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: Conventional high-entropy alloy intermediate layers with largely random grain orientations and isotropic microstructures that show limited directional heat conduction and marginal heat-transfer performance.
generation.intervention: Apply directional solidification coupled with aligned thermo-mechanical processing to induce an interconnected, channelled lamellar microstructure oriented along the anticipated heat-flux direction.
generation.conditions: High-temperature and high-stress reactor conditions, such as temperatures exceeding 500°C and exposure to extreme thermal flux and cyclic mechanical loading typical of plasma-facing environments.
generation.structural_mediator: Aligned, lamellar microstructure providing continuous high-conductivity channels with coherent interfaces that distribute stress effectively.
generation.mechanism: The induced directional microstructure creates preferential pathways that enhance heat conduction along the lamellae while maintaining coherent interfaces. This alignment minimizes thermal gradients and mitigates localized stress concentrations, thereby preserving mechanical integrity.
generation.predicted_outcome: The engineered alloy is expected to exhibit a statistically significant improvement in directional thermal conductivity (e.g., an enhancement >20% along the channel direction relative to untreated controls) without compromising yield strength and ductility under reactor operating conditions.
generation.baseline: Standard high-entropy alloy intermediate layers show suboptimal directional heat-transfer capability and a trade-off between thermal conductivity and mechanical robustness.
generation.boundary: The anticipated benefits are limited to microstructural improvements achieved within the standard compositional framework and processing parameters; drastic composition changes or processing deviations may not reproduce the effect.
generation.uncertainty: While directional solidification is known to refine and align microstructures, the exact quantitative improvement in thermal conductivity and potential anisotropic responses in mechanical properties under extreme conditions require further experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sample sets of high-entropy alloy intermediate layers: one processed with standard techniques and one with the proposed directional solidification and aligned thermo-mechanical processing. Subject both sets to simulated plasma-facing reactor environments that impose high thermal loads (>500°C) and mechanical cyclic stress.
measurements: Measure directional thermal conductivity (along vs perpendicular to the lamellar channels) using a laser flash apparatus or equivalent method.
Assess mechanical properties (yield strength, ductility, and toughness) via high-temperature tensile and compression tests.
Characterize microstructure orientation and coherence through SEM/TEM imaging.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the processed samples do not show at least a 20% enhancement in directional thermal conductivity compared to controls or if their mechanical properties (e.g., yield strength and ductility) decline by more than 10% under test conditions, then the hypothesis will be falsified.

The results indicate that the microstructure of the alloy after directional solidification treatment transforms from dendritic crystals to columnar crystals or even single crystals. The fracture strength of the alloy has been significantly improved, with an 80% increase in strength compared to the alloy obtained by ordinary casting. Therefore, the use of arc additive manufacturing technology can achieve directional solidification of high-entropy alloys. It can be seen that previous studies have largely focused on the research of different elemental contents in high-entropy alloys and the effects of these varying elemental contents on intermetallic compounds. The underlying origin lying behind the observed mechanical response is the inherited lamellar geometry from the as-cast EHEA. It is known that grain refinement to the nano/ultrafine-grained regime can render material stronger, but this process is usually accompanied by a dramatic loss of ductility. However, with a composite lamellar architecture, the ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure in this study achieves an improved strength–ductility synergy. decision.trend: Early work in high‐entropy alloys has largely aimed at tailoring the microstructure to boost mechanical properties. For example, PMC6353877 demonstrated how processing (casting–rolling–annealing) can yield ultrafine duplex lamellar architectures that improve strength–ductility synergy, while PMC10213035 employed controllable coherent nanoprecipitations in tungsten‐based HEAs to achieve ultrahigh strength and ductility suitable for plasma‐facing components. In both cases, the focus was on addressing the trade-off between mechanical performance and processing challenges under extreme temperature and stress. However, despite these successes, conventional formulations still fall short when it comes to engineered heat-transfer capability, leaving a gap in creating in situ composite microstructures that serve as efficient thermal conduits without compromising structural integrity.
decision.unsolved: The persistent challenge is to improve the heat-transfer capability—specifically, to create continuous conduction pathways within the HEA intermediate layer that can efficiently handle extreme thermal flux—while retaining or enhancing mechanical robustness in plasma‐facing reactor conditions. The microstructural designs explored so far have not been optimized for directional thermal transport.
decision.lever: Directional solidification followed by aligned thermo-mechanical processing to induce an interconnected, lamellar (or channelled) microstructure oriented along the expected heat flux.
decision.why: Building on the positive impact of engineered lamellar architectures on mechanical properties (as shown in PMC6353877) and the robust performance of tungsten refractory HEAs in plasma‐facing applications (PMC10213035), this intervention logically extends previous trends. By using directional processing to align high-conductivity channels, one can create percolating paths for heat transfer while retaining coherent interfaces that ensure structural integrity. This single, process-based intervention directly targets the dual requirement of enhanced heat transfer and maintained mechanical performance.

families.principle: Tailoring the electronic and phononic transport by adjusting the alloy composition to optimize free-electron density and scatterings.
cues_for: prior attempts used standard formulations without targeted modifications
cues_against: Potential composition changes might adversely affect the balance of strength if not finely controlled
families.best_lever: Incorporate a minor addition of a high thermal conductivity element (e.g., trace Cu) designed to boost electron transport without destabilizing the disordered matrix.

families.best_lever: Apply a calibrated annealing cycle designed to optimize phase distribution and grain boundary character to favor thermal transport without sacrificing strength.

families.principle: Modifying the surface or interfacial regions to reduce thermal boundary resistance and improve overall thermal conduction between layers.
cues_for: Plasma-facing reactor components involve multiple interfaces where improved thermal transfer can be crucial

This intervention might not address the internal trade-off between heat transfer and structural integrity directly
families.best_lever: Introduce an engineered interfacial nanolayer that minimizes contact resistance, though its impact is more extrinsic and may be secondary to bulk modifications.
